dedupe_keys.name: netrainsim open source network freight train simulator

description: NeTrainSim is an open-source simulator of train operations on large rail networks. It models freight train longitudinal motion and energy consumption second by second for each train, with train dynamics that include operator aggressiveness, an energy consumption module for a range of train technologies and an energy optimisation module under development, and it can simulate networks up to country scale. It was developed by Ahmed Aredah, Karim Fadhloun and Hesham Rakha at the Virginia Tech Transportation Institute and described in a 2024 Railway Engineering Science article under CC BY 4.0. It is generic and can be adapted to any rail network described as nodes, links and trains. It is built with Qt6 and released under GPL version 3 on GitHub with a Windows installer that bundles its dependencies, a graphical interface and a command-line interface whose required inputs are node, link and train files. Caveats: the ready-made installer targets Windows, the optimisation module is unfinished, and results depend on the network and train data supplied. NeTrainSim supports rail network capacity and energy studies, decarbonisation scenarios for freight rail and testing of operational changes. It complements OpenTrack and the other rail simulators catalogued here.
